target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (T : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓢 T → Def2 𝓢 T → (∃ lam, 𝓢 ⊢ lam 🡘 ∼T lam) → 𝓢 ⊢ ⊥
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is defined to be the following proposition: For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm and provability relation for S on Fm, every system 𝓢 of type S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, and every function T from Fm to Fm: if (1) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication from φ to T(φ); if also (2) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication from T(φ) to φ; and if also (3) there exists a sentence lam such that 𝓢 proves the biconditional between lam and the negation of T(lam), then 𝓢 proves falsehood. The implications in (1) and (2) are themselves proved sentences, not merely rules taking proofs to proofs. In (3), lam need not be identical to the negation of T(lam), and neither side of the biconditional is separately required to be provable. No consistency assumption is made."}
translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition: For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm and provability relation for S on Fm, every system 𝓢 of type S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens, and every function T from Fm to Fm: if (1) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication from φ to T(φ); if also (2) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the implication from T(φ) to φ; and if also (3) there exists a sentence lam such that 𝓢 proves the biconditional between lam and the negation of T(lam), then 𝓢 proves falsehood. The implications in (1) and (2) are themselves proved sentences, not merely rules taking proofs to proofs. In (3), lam need not be identical to the negation of T(lam), and neither side of the biconditional is separately required to be provable. No consistency assumption is made.

divergences.description: The passage asserts inconsistency after adding both T-In and K-Intro. The target gives a stronger sufficient condition: given T-Out and a provable liar biconditional, T-In suffices without K-Intro. This is the author's stated strengthening, not a claim explicitly made in the passage.

The target concerns any classical system satisfying the hypotheses, rather than constructing DTK extended by T-In. It takes T-Out and the liar biconditional as hypotheses; their availability in the DTK extension, including the arithmetic coding behind the liar, is not established by the target.

judgement.summary: The target faithfully supports the stated remark: at the liar sentence, T-In and T-Out give a provable equivalence with its truth assertion, while the liar biconditional gives a provable equivalence with the negation of that assertion. In a classical system these entail provable falsehood.
